extracted.intended_audience: AI researchers and practitioners working on LLM-based autonomous agents and planning
extracted.subtask_description: A survey paper that provides a taxonomy and comprehensive analyses of approaches for planning in LLM-powered autonomous agents, covering methods aimed at improving planning ability and discussing open challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Decomposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one category in the paper's taxonomy of LLM-Agent planning approaches. Implicitly refers to methods that break down tasks into subtasks/subgoals to improve LLM planning ability. The paper states it conducts comprehensive analyses of this direction and discusses related challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan Selection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One category in the taxonomy; refers to approaches that select among candidate plans generated by LLMs or external modules to choose effective action sequences. The survey analyzes recent works in this direction and highlights open problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Module
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A taxonomy category indicating the use of external, non-LLM modules to support planning (e.g., symbolic planners, search modules, tool-using components). The paper provides analyses of works using external modules to improve planning ability and discusses associated challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named category in the survey taxonomy; refers to techniques where LLMs iteratively reflect on, revise, or self-evaluate plans to improve outcomes. The paper analyzes reflection-based methods and their role in enhancing planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as a taxonomy category; covers mechanisms for storing and retrieving context, past plans, or experiences to inform planning decisions. The survey examines memory-oriented approaches and their impact on planning performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve planning ability (overall objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: The survey covers recent works aiming to improve planning ability of LLM-based agents and provides a taxonomy of approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's organizing principle and evaluative lens: works are grouped and assessed by how they contribute to improving planning (via the five directions above). It states that comprehensive analyses are conducted for each direction and further challenges for the field are discussed.
